title: Homotoping a distribution to a foliation
statement: For a smooth codimension-\(n\) distribution \(D\subset TM\), determine whether it can be homotoped through distributions of the same rank to an integrable distribution. Bott’s necessary condition is the vanishing over \(\mathbb R\) of every Pontryagin monomial of \(TM/D\) whose cohomological degree exceeds \(2n\).
status: As of November 2026, the Bott obstruction is established. The present occurrence supplies its formal-vector-field interpretation; the checked sources do not turn this necessary condition into a general sufficiency criterion \citep{bott1970integrability,bott1976characteristic}.

title: Critical exponents of finite-dimensional lp norms
statement: For fixed \(n\) and \(1\le p<\infty\), over the real and complex scalar fields separately, does every norm-one contraction on \(\ell_p^n\) that preserves norm through a bounded number of powers have spectral radius one? Equivalently, is \(q(\ell_p^n)<\infty\)?
status: As of November 2026, the verified result is finiteness for every rational \(p\), already proved before the talk by \citet[Theorem 1, Corollaries 2--3]{kirzhnertabachnikov1971critical}. The exact later fate for irrational \(p\) and optimal bounds was not established in this search; absence of a verified successor is not asserted to mean current openness.

title: Growth of the minimum critical exponent over all norms
statement: For a fixed scalar field let \(M(n)=\min_{\dim E=n}q(E)\). Must \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}M(n)=\infty\)?
status: As of November 2026, the Hilbert bound \(M(n)\le n\) is verified, but neither the notebook’s claimed square-root subsequence construction nor the precise later resolution of the lower-growth question was identified. The similarly named 1995 exponential-number invariant does not answer this question.

title: Maximizing a power norm under a spectral-radius constraint
statement: For a specified finite-dimensional normed space \(E\), determine \(C(E,r,\rho)=\max\{\|T^r\|:\|T\|\le1,\ r(T)\le\rho\}\), including sharp bounds and extremizers, for \(r\ge1\), \(0\le\rho<1\).
status: As of November 2026, compactness gives existence of the maximum and the critical exponent characterizes when it is strictly below one for every fixed \(\rho<1\). This does not evaluate the maximum. The exact state of the optimization problem for arbitrary norms was not verified; specific Pták operator results must be matched separately.

title: Geometric computation of spectral flow
statement: For a closed family of self-adjoint elliptic operators, compute its signed eigenvalue flow from the family symbol and geometric gluing data; in first order, identify it with the index of the suspended mapping-torus operator.
status: Solved in the elliptic setting by the topological-index formula and suspension equality of \citet[Theorem 7.4, pp.~94--95]{atiyahpatodisinger1976spectral3}. The notebook supplies September 1971 circulation evidence; publication followed in 1976. As of November 2026 the required hypotheses and distinction from arbitrary nonlocal unitary gluing are standard.

title: Normalized universal relations among elementary matrices
statement: Let \(R=\mathbb Z\langle X\rangle\) be the free associative unital ring, augmented to \(\mathbb Z\) by \(X\mapsto0\). Does \(\ker(K_2(R)\to K_2(\mathbb Z))\) vanish? Equivalently, is every universally valid stable elementary matrix relation whose Steinberg lift specializes to the identity under augmentation a consequence of the Steinberg relations? The normalization is necessary; arbitrary constant relations include the nonzero \(K_2(\mathbb Z)\).
status: As of November 2026: resolved in the stated augmented formulation. Vaserstein announces the answer in the March 1972 notebook and the free-ring theorem in \citet[second theorem]{vaserstein1973foundations}; \citet[Theorem 28.1 and Corollary 28.1]{vaserstein1976foundations} gives its precise reduced formulation. The February notebook omits the augmentation condition, so the match is qualified rather than an assertion that every unnormalized relation is trivial. No exact earlier recurrence was found in the supplied prior index.

title: Agreement of the early higher algebraic K-theory constructions
statement: For every associative unital ring \(A\) and every \(n\ge1\), do the stable simplicial constructions of Volodin and Vaserstein and the free-resolution constructions of Swan and Gersten agree naturally with \(\pi_nBGL(A)^+\)? One concrete consequence asked in the notes is the Quillen-theory suspension isomorphism \(K_{n+1}(\Sigma A)\cong K_n(A)\). Polynomial-homotopy Karoubi--Villamayor groups are excluded without additional regularity.
status: As of November 2026: resolved for the specified stable constructions and unital rings. The spring 1972 seminar announcement is documented by \citet[introduction, p.97]{vaserstein1976foundations}; \citet[first theorem]{vaserstein1973foundations} publishes the comparison, with the detailed Quillen and free-resolution arguments in the 1976 paper, \S\S27--29. Record 257's catalogue attribution is conditional and does not create an additional independent priority claim. No exact earlier problem identifier was located in the supplied index.

title: Unitary equivalence modulo trace class from spectral data
statement: For bounded self-adjoint operators \(A,B\) on separable Hilbert spaces, characterize from their spectral measures and multiplicities whether \(A-UBU^*\in\mathcal S_1\) for some unitary \(U\).
status: As of November 2026, the subject has a dedicated later classification literature and the purely singular diagonalization case is verified indirectly. This audit has not independently checked the complete necessary-and-sufficient criterion for a prescribed pair of spectral types, and does not assert that equality of absolutely continuous parts alone suffices.

title: The exceptional exponent 26 in the eta identities
statement: Explain the \(\eta^{26}\) identity in root-system terms despite the absence of a simple complex Lie algebra of dimension 26.
status: As of November 2026, resolved in the affine-root framework: the dual-root specialization for \(F_4\) is described by \citet[Section I, pp. 200--201]{monastyrskii1980appendix}.
